findings.title: Team admin check requires owner role too (&& instead of ||)
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, so only a user who is both admin and owner passes. Plain team admins are rejected with FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name says admin-or-owner and the UI shows the 'additional guests' action for any booking in the list. The operator should be `||`.

findings.title: Guest blacklist is bypassed by uppercase email addresses
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased when built (line 71), but the incoming `guest` is compared as-is with `includes(guest)`. An input such as `Spammer@Blocked.example` is not matched against a blacklisted `spammer@blocked.example`. The guest is then inserted as an attendee and receives an invitation sent in the organizer's name. The guest should be lowercased before the comparison.

findings.title: Duplicate guests in one request are not rejected server-side
findings.body: The `uniqueGuests` filter only removes emails that already match an existing attendee, using a case-sensitive comparison. It does not dedupe within `guests`. The uniqueness refinement exists only in the client dialog, and the zod schema does not enforce it. A direct API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` or `["A@x.com","a@x.com"]` creates duplicate attendee rows via `createMany` and sends duplicate invitations.

findings.title: Attendees are committed before the calendar update, which is not guarded
findings.body: The attendees are written to the DB at lines 92-106, then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs with no try/catch. If the calendar call throws, the new attendees stay in the database, the calendar is not updated, no emails are sent, and the user sees an error. A retry is then rejected at lines 80-81 because those emails now match existing attendees, so the calendar invite can never be sent through this flow. The DB write and the calendar update need to be ordered, compensated, or made transactional.

findings.title: Raw `guests` input passed to email sender instead of the filtered list
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the original request list, not `uniqueGuests`. Any address in the request that is already an attendee (or blacklisted) matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in `sendAddGuestsEmails`. That attendee then receives a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` invitation as if newly added, instead of the 'guests added' email. Passing `uniqueGuests` fixes this.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed without logging the error
findings.body: The catch block discards `err` and writes a fixed `console.log` string. The error is lost, and the mutation still returns success, so a failed email send is hard to diagnose. The error should be logged with the logger, including `err`.

findings.title: No cap on number of guests; any attendee is authorized
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`. Each guest triggers a DB insert, a calendar update, and an invitation email with an ICS attachment sent in the organizer's name. The handler also allows any user whose email matches an existing attendee (addGuests.handler.ts lines 52-54) to do this. A single attendee could send unlimited invitations to arbitrary addresses through the platform's mail infrastructure. A reasonable limit on the array size is needed.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other send function in this file checks `hostEmailDisabled` / `attendeeEmailDisabled` or `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` before sending. `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends unconditionally to the organizer, team members, and attendees. It takes no metadata parameter, and the handler does not pass one. Event types where the organizer disabled standard emails will still receive 'guests added' emails.

findings.title: Misleading error when all guests are already attendees or blacklisted
findings.body: When every submitted email is already an attendee or is blacklisted, the handler throws `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which reads as 'Emails must be unique and valid'. A valid address that is already on the booking therefore gets an error suggesting the input is malformed. A specific message such as 'guests already added' would be accurate.

findings.title: Check-then-insert race can create duplicate attendees
findings.body: The existing-attendee check reads `booking.attendees` at lines 26-42, then `createMany` runs at lines 92-106 with no transaction and no uniqueness constraint on (booking, email). Two concurrent requests (double submit or two tabs) can both pass the filter and insert the same guest twice, producing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails.

findings.title: Error toast shows raw tRPC code and the fallback is unreachable
findings.body: The message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, so users see text like 'BAD_REQUEST: Emails must be unique and valid'. Because the template always contains ': ', `message` is never falsy, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is dead code. The toast should show the translated message, with the fallback applied explicitly when there is no message.

findings.title: isInvalidEmail error persists after closing or succeeding
findings.body: `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is set on validation failure but only reset by the Cancel button (line 91). It is not reset in `onSuccess` (line 39) or when the dialog is dismissed via the X or Escape. The stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' message appears the next time the dialog opens, even though the input was cleared.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip text bypasses i18n
findings.body: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` is a literal English string, while the rest of the component uses `t()`. Users in other locales see English text for this control, and the string is not in the locale files.

findings.title: No tests for the new permission, dedupe, blacklist, or email-routing logic
findings.body: The handler contains authorization branching, the guest filtering and blacklist logic, and the calendar and email side effects, but no tests are added. The AND-vs-OR permission bug, the blacklist case bypass, and the wrong email list passed to the sender would all be caught by unit tests. The dialog and the email templates are also untested.
